LESSON: GROWING VEGETABLES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESSES Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested
Topic 2.1: Growing vegetables
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 9

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Growing vegetables, part of FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESSES Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How does growing vegetables contribute to food production?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Growing vegetables together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Social justice: The learner shares tasks with the partner as they sow vegetable seed.

Responsibility: The learner develops accountability as they handle the school tools responsibly when planting and growing their own

vegetables and observes safety precautions while using the tools.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
13

Financial literacy: The learner exhibits financial literacy skills by reducing daily vegetable purchases.

Link to other subjects:

Mathematics: Learner uses the skills of measurements for correct spacing while growing the crops.

Suggested learning resources:

• Print and non-print materials.

• Nursery bed- small piece of land or Containers like old buckets, barrels split in half.

• Farming tools- sticks, watering cans, pangas, jembes,

• Variety of vegetable seeds.

• Source of water.

• Digital devices.
